newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South Africa's currency and gilt markets took timeout on Friday after a hectic week in which the rand firmed almost four cents against the dollar and yields fell nearly 30 basis points.

At the Friday close, the rand was pegged at 4.5635/5665 against the dollar from 4.5615/5745 overnight. It began the week at just over 4.60 and touched a two-month high of 4.5525 bid against the dollar on Thursday.
"The market has basically taken a bit of a break after a pretty rough week," a dealer said.

Dealers said that on the day, the currency had drifted between the 4.56 and 4.57 levels with importers preventing any significant advance below 4.56 and exporters and offshore dollar sellers halting the rand's attempts to move weaker.
"It has been stuck down at 4.56 with nowhere to go," a trader said.

Dealers said that in the week ahead, the currency could resume its rally against the dollar, although some dealers the fact that the currency had failed to successfully breach the key 4.55 chart level during the week signalled more of the same next week.

"It is difficult to call," a dealer said. "We have sat here for the last three or four days and haven't done anything so we might see a bit of profit-taking." He added that there were perceptions that the currency looked overbought at current levels.
Another trader said the currency appeared to be trading more on technicals at the moment, having discounted most of the other positive fundamentals in the market.
He said the currency needed move back up to the 4.5850 level before it could strengthen again.
Against the crosses, the rand firmed against the British pound to trade at 7.3064/3158 from 7.3918/4013 on Thursday, but weakened slightly against the mark to 0.3586/3590 from 0.3590/3593 previously.
On the bond market, yields finally pierced the 15.25 percent level which dealers have pointed to all week as a key chart level, but failed to make significant progress beyond there.

At the local finish, the key R150 was pegged at a 15.25 percent compared with 15.31 percent on Friday after trading at a three-month low of 15.225 percent. The gilt started the week at 15.465 percent.
"It's been a very quiet day...most people were watching cricket," a dealer said in reference to a match being played between South Africa and Zimbabwe in Johannesburg.
Dealers said that the move through 15.25 percent was sparked earlier by developments on the money market, where the shortage continued to confound month-end pressures.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage plunged 1.4 billion rand on Thursday to 7.089 billion rand from 8.490 billion rand on Wednesday.

Money market rates reflected the easing liquidity pressures by falling further. Three-month NCDs were quoted by South Africa's four major banks at between 16.55 and 16.60 percent offered from 16.90 to 16.95 percent offered on Thursday.
The 90-day BA rate fell to between 15.95 percent and 16.15 percent bid.
Bond traders said that in the coming week, the market was expected to continue stronger, although volatility could increase with options close-out looming on Thursday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 98.3 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 99.16 million rands worth on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Thursday -- a settlement date -- was 35.09 billion rand from 7.23 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
